data.definition: Inspired or permeated with a feeling, quality, or idea.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'with' after 'imbued'.
examples: His writings are imbued with deep philosophical wisdom.
The culture is imbued with respect for elders.
data.common_mistake: ❌ The tradition is imbued by religious meaning. ➜ ✅ The tradition is imbued with religious meaning.

data.definition: Protected or exempt from legal prosecution, penalty, or burden.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'immune from' for legal protection/prosecution, and 'immune to' for diseases/criticism.
examples: Diplomats are often immune from local criminal prosecution.
The president is immune from civil lawsuits while in office.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He is immune against legal action. ➜ ✅ He is immune from legal action.

data.definition: Resistant to a particular infection, toxin, or negative influence.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'immune to' when protected against diseases, criticism, or persuasion.
examples: Vaccinated individuals are largely immune to the virus.
Nobody is completely immune to criticism.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He is immune from feedback. ➜ ✅ He is immune to feedback.

data.pattern: be + impervious to + [pain / rain / criticism / reason]
data.definition: Not allowing fluid to pass through; unable to be affected or penetrated.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'impervious to' for physical waterproofing or mental resistance to influence.
examples: This raincoat is completely impervious to water.
He seemed impervious to reason and common sense.
data.common_mistake: ❌ The wall is impervious from water. ➜ ✅ The wall is impervious to water.

data.definition: Of great significance or value.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'important for' (benefit/welfare) or 'important to' (personal value/feeling).
examples: Regular exercise is important for maintaining physical health.
Family traditions are very important to her.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Fresh food is important of kids. ➜ ✅ Fresh food is important for kids.

data.definition: Not having the ability, fitness, or capacity to achieve something.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'of' after 'incapable' followed by a gerund (-ing). Never use 'to' + base verb.
examples: The machine is incapable of processing high-volume requests.
He seemed incapable of telling the truth.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He is incapable to understand. ➜ ✅ He is incapable of understanding.

data.definition: Opposed in character; incapable of existing together in harmony.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'with' after 'incompatible'.
examples: His radical ideas are incompatible with company policy.
The new app is incompatible with older phones.
data.common_mistake: ❌ The software is incompatible to my laptop. ➜ ✅ The software is incompatible with my laptop.

data.definition: Serving as a sign or indication of something.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'of' after 'indicative'. Do NOT use 'about' or 'for'.
examples: High turnover rates are indicative of poor workplace morale.
Her rapid progress is indicative of strong dedication.
data.common_mistake: ❌ The fever is indicative for infection. ➜ ✅ The fever is indicative of infection.

data.definition: Having no particular interest or sympathy; unconcerned.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'to' after 'indifferent'. Do NOT use 'about' or 'with'.
examples: He seemed completely indifferent to her suffering.
She is indifferent to public opinion.
data.common_mistake: ❌ They are indifferent about politics. ➜ ✅ They are indifferent to politics.

data.definition: Lacking concern, warmth, or interest toward a topic or individual.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'indifferent toward' or 'indifferent to'.
examples: The government remained indifferent toward public protests.
She was indifferent toward fashion trends.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He is indifferent for feedback. ➜ ✅ He is indifferent toward feedback.

data.definition: Feeling or showing anger or annoyance at what is perceived as unfair treatment.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'indignant at', 'indignant about', or 'indignant over'.
examples: Citizens were indignant at the unfair tax increase.
She became indignant about the false allegations.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He was indignant with the decision. ➜ ✅ He was indignant at the decision.

data.definition: Lower in rank, quality, or status.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'to' after 'inferior'. Never use 'than'.
examples: Synthetic leather is often inferior to genuine leather.
No one should feel inferior to others.
data.common_mistake: ❌ The quality is inferior than expected. ➜ ✅ The quality is inferior to expected standards.

data.definition: Filled, pervaded, or soaked with a quality or principle.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'with' after 'infused'.
examples: His speeches were always infused with passion and humor.
The tea is infused with natural berry flavors.
data.common_mistake: ❌ The essay was infused by enthusiasm. ➜ ✅ The essay was infused with enthusiasm.

data.definition: Existing in something as a permanent, essential, or characteristic attribute.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'in' after 'inherent'. Do NOT use 'to'.
examples: Stress is an inherent risk in high-pressure medical jobs.
Inequality was inherent in the old feudal system.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Danger is inherent to extreme sports. ➜ ✅ Danger is inherent in extreme sports.

data.definition: Necessary to make a whole complete; essential or fundamental.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'to' after 'integral'.
examples: Regular practice is integral to mastering a foreign language.
Security is integral to our software design.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Trust is integral for a relationship. ➜ ✅ Trust is integral to a relationship.

data.definition: Feeling curiosity or concern about something.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'in' after 'interested'. Follow with a noun or gerund (-ing).
examples: Are you interested in learning new languages?
She is interested in modern art.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He is interested about science. ➜ ✅ He is interested in science.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Adjective: 'interested in history' ➔ Related Noun: 'take an interest in history'

data.definition: Belonging naturally; essential to the basic nature of something.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'intrinsic to' or 'intrinsic in'.
examples: Curiosity is intrinsic to human nature.
Risks are intrinsic in financial markets.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Creativity is intrinsic for design. ➜ ✅ Creativity is intrinsic to design.

data.definition: Resistance to a disease or protection from legal burden.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'immunity TO' diseases, and 'immunity FROM' prosecution.
examples: Vaccines build long-term immunity to contagious diseases.
The witness was granted immunity from prosecution.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Immunity against prosecution. ➜ ✅ Immunity from prosecution.

data.definition: A marked effect or influence.
data.grammar_rule: The noun 'impact ON' takes 'on'. Contrast with verb 'impact' (often direct object in formal prose).
examples: Technology has had a huge impact on modern communication.
Scientists studied the asteroid's impact on climate.
data.common_mistake: ❌ It has an impact to our community. ➜ ✅ It has an impact on our community.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'an impact ON the economy' ➔ Verb: 'impact'

data.definition: An idea, feeling, or opinion of something or someone, formed without conscious thought.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'impression OF' someone/something.
examples: What was your first impression of the new manager?
The city left a lasting impression of elegance on us.
data.common_mistake: ❌ My impression about Paris. ➜ ✅ My impression of Paris.

data.definition: The state of two things being so different as to be incapable of existing together.
data.grammar_rule: Matches adjective 'incompatible with'.
examples: Software incompatibility with the operating system caused crashes.
Marital incompatibility led to divorce.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Incompatibility to old versions. ➜ ✅ Incompatibility with old versions.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'incompatibility WITH company culture' ➔ Adjective: 'incompatible with'

data.definition: The fact or state of being inconsistent.
data.grammar_rule: Matches adjective 'inconsistent with' and contrast 'consistent with'.
examples: Lawyers pointed out an inconsistency with his previous statement.
Quality inconsistency with factory standards was noted.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Inconsistency to the truth. ➜ ✅ Inconsistency with the truth.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'inconsistency WITH the evidence' ➔ Adjective: 'consistent with'

data.definition: A rise in the amount, size, or degree of something.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'increase IN' before the concept rising (e.g. increase in sales). Contrast with 'increase BY' for the amount (increased by 10%).
examples: There has been a sharp increase in house prices.
We noticed an increase in website traffic.
data.common_mistake: ❌ An increase of the price. ➜ ✅ An increase in the price.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'an increase IN sales' ➔ Verb: 'sales increased by 10%'

data.definition: A formal charge or accusation of a serious crime, OR a severe condemnation.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'indictment OF'.
examples: The report was a damning indictment of prison conditions.
High poverty rates are an indictment of state failure.
data.common_mistake: ❌ An indictment on the administration. ➜ ✅ An indictment of the administration.

data.definition: Lack of interest, concern, or sympathy.
data.grammar_rule: Matches adjective 'indifferent to'.
examples: His callous indifference to the feelings of others shocked everyone.
Consumer indifference to advertising is rising.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Indifference about politics. ➜ ✅ Indifference to politics.

data.definition: The capacity to have an effect on the character, development, or behavior of someone or something.
data.grammar_rule: The noun 'influence ON' takes 'on'. Contrast with the transitive verb 'influence' which takes a direct object with NO preposition.
examples: Parents have a profound influence on their children's values.
His musical style was a strong influence on jazz.
data.common_mistake: ❌ He has an influence over me. ➜ ✅ He has an influence on me.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'have an influence ON children' ➔ Verb: 'influence' (no prep)

data.definition: The action of breaking the terms of a law or agreement, or encroaching on rights.
data.grammar_rule: Matches verb 'infringe on'. Use 'infringement ON/UPON' (or 'infringement OF copyright').
examples: Surveillance laws represent an infringement on personal privacy.
The company faced lawsuits for copyright infringement.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Infringement against rights. ➜ ✅ Infringement on rights.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'infringement ON civil liberties' ➔ Verb: 'infringe on'

data.definition: An official investigation to establish facts.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'inquiry INTO'. Matches verb 'look into'.
examples: Parliament ordered a public inquiry into the bank failure.
An independent inquiry into the accident is underway.
data.common_mistake: ❌ An inquiry about the scandal. ➜ ✅ An inquiry into the scandal.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'an inquiry INTO the crash' ➔ Verb: 'look into'

data.definition: An accurate and deep intuitive understanding of a person or thing.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'insight INTO'. Do NOT use 'about' or 'on'.
examples: The research provides fascinating insight into whale communication.
Her biography gives a rare insight into her personal life.
data.common_mistake: ❌ An insight about human behavior. ➜ ✅ An insight into human behavior.

data.definition: The feeling of wanting to know or learn about something.
data.grammar_rule: The noun 'interest IN' takes 'in'. This matches the adjective 'interested in'.
examples: He has a keen interest in computer programming.
Her interest in photography started early.
data.common_mistake: ❌ She has an interest about music. ➜ ✅ She has an interest in music.
data.related_forms: ⚡ Noun: 'take an interest IN science' ➔ Adjective: 'interested in'

data.definition: The action of investigating something or someone; formal examination.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'investigation INTO'.
examples: Police launched a thorough investigation into the fraud allegation.
An investigation into the cause of the fire was initiated.
data.common_mistake: ❌ An investigation of the crash (formal: INTO). ➜ ✅ An investigation into the crash.

data.definition: A written or spoken request inviting someone to attend an event.
data.grammar_rule: Always use 'to' after 'invitation'. Do NOT use 'for'.
examples: Did you receive an invitation to Sarah's wedding?
Thank you for the kind invitation to dinner.
data.common_mistake: ❌ An invitation for the party arrived today. ➜ ✅ An invitation to the party arrived today.

data.definition: To feel a strong connection or affinity.
data.grammar_rule: Requires 'with' when expressing empathy/connection.
examples: I identify with the main character.
Many people identify with this story.
data.common_mistake: ❌ I identify to this character. ➔ ✅ I identify with this character.

data.definition: To form a mental image or concept.
data.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb without preposition.
examples: Imagine a world without war.
I can't imagine living there.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Imagine about a quiet place. ➔ ✅ Imagine a quiet place.

data.definition: To have a strong effect or influence on someone or something.
data.grammar_rule: As a verb, 'impact' can take a direct object or 'on'. As a noun, it always takes 'on'.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'This policy impacts local business' ➔ Noun: 'This policy has an impact ON local business'
examples: The decision will impact on future generations.
Technology heavily impacts our daily routines.
data.common_mistake: ❌ A negative impact for society. ➔ ✅ A negative impact on society.

data.definition: To encroach or have an intrusive effect on someone's rights or privacy.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable formal verb requiring 'on' or 'upon'.
examples: The proposed surveillance law impinges on personal privacy.
New regulations must not impinge upon academic freedom.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Impinge to civil liberties. ➔ ✅ Impinge on civil liberties.

data.definition: Having control of or responsibility for a department, team, or task.
data.grammar_rule: Prepositional idiom requiring OF + noun or gerund (-ing). Use FOR when expressing purpose separately.
examples: She's in charge of setting the company's vision and goals.
Who is in charge of handling client contracts?
data.common_mistake: ❌ In charge for setting goals. ➔ ✅ In charge of setting goals.

data.definition: To allow oneself to enjoy the pleasure of something, often excessively.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable verb + preposition structure requiring 'in'.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Indulge in sweets' ➔ Noun: 'Self-indulgence IN sweets'
examples: On weekends she likes to indulge in a long spa day.
They indulged in luxury shopping during their vacation.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Indulge with fine dining. ➔ ✅ Indulge in fine dining.

data.definition: To have an effect on the character, development, or behavior of someone or something.
data.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb without preposition! Do NOT use 'on' after the verb 'influence'. However, the noun 'influence' DOES take 'on'.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'It influences me' (no prep) ➔ Noun: 'It has an influence ON me' (uses ON)
examples: Weather can strongly influence people's mood.
His speeches influenced millions of voters.
data.common_mistake: ❌ It influences on my decision. ➔ ✅ It influences my decision. (OR: It has an influence on my decision.)

data.definition: To violate or trespass upon a law, right, or agreement.
data.grammar_rule: Inseparable legal verb taking 'on' or 'upon'.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Infringe on copyright' ➔ Noun: 'An infringement ON copyright'
examples: Copying this software infringes on patent rights.
Do not infringe upon the freedom of speech.
data.common_mistake: ❌ Infringe against my copyright. ➔ ✅ Infringe on my copyright.

data.definition: To embed decorative material.
examples: Artisans inlay wood with ivory.
Craftsman inlaid gold pattern table.
Jewels have been inlaid in crown.

data.definition: To demand something forcefully and refuse to accept any refusal.
data.grammar_rule: Requires 'on' + gerund (-ing) or noun object.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'insist on paying' ➔ Noun: 'an insistence ON quality'
examples: He insisted on paying for everyone's dinner.
Why do you insist on doing everything by yourself?
data.common_mistake: ❌ Insist to pay the bill. ➔ ✅ Insist on paying the bill.

data.definition: To hinder or disrupt a process, or meddle in private affairs.
data.grammar_rule: Use 'interfere with' for disruption of processes, and 'interfere in' for unwanted intrusion into affairs.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Interfere with work' ➔ Noun: 'Interference WITH work'
examples: Loud music can interfere with your concentration.
Stop trying to interfere in my personal life!
data.common_mistake: ❌ Interfere to my business. ➔ ✅ Interfere in my business.

data.definition: To put money, time, or energy into something for future benefit.
data.grammar_rule: Intransitive investment verb requiring 'in' before the asset or venture.
data.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Invest in stocks' ➔ Noun: 'Make an investment IN stocks'
examples: The company is investing in renewable energy technology.
It is wise to invest in employee training.
data.common_mistake: ❌ They invested on real estate. ➔ ✅ They invested in real estate.
